The '''Union Alphabet''' is the standardized writing system source-attested for the [[Union of Zhensanov]] and the [[Zhensanovian Languages]].

== Development ==

Source material says the alphabet was developed in the mid-twentieth century as part of the [[Union Language Committee]]'s effort to create a writing system that could represent sounds across Zhensanovian languages. Its goals included phonemic coverage, learnability, cultural neutrality, and support for official and educational use.

The exact adoption year, legislative process, and relationship to existing regional scripts are not yet known.

== Structure And Use ==

The source describes the Union Alphabet as a left-to-right alphabet with forty-five base letters and diacritics. It is designed for government documents, education materials, public signage, media publications, and broader official communication in the source set, but the exact pre-1994 adoption scope remains open.

Because the extracted glyph tables contain corrupted characters and later digital references, this draft preserves the high-level structure and policy role without hardening the full character inventory for publication.

== Canon Limits ==

The Sanovic source later ties the Union Alphabet to a constructed Union lingua franca, but Sanovic itself is described as an early twenty-first-century language. For the 1994-back pass, the Union Alphabet is therefore treated as a pre-1994 script-standardization project for Zhensanovian languages, while Sanovic belongs to later review.
